title: AI Adoption and Firms' Job-Posting Behavior (Liu and Webber)
key_claim: Federal Reserve analysis of US firm-level AI adoption and labor demand documents shifts in skill mix and posting volume linked to AI integration; primary federal-government empirical analysis of how AI is reshaping job postings and skills demand.
notes: Federal Reserve Notes — Tier 1 primary research / regulator analysis.

title: Speech by Governor Barr on Artificial Intelligence and the Labor Market
key_claim: Governor Barr's analytical commentary on AI labor market effects: 35.9% of US workers using generative AI by December 2025; small positive wage effects observed; no statistically significant declines in job openings or employment in exposed occupations to date.
notes: Federal Reserve Governor speech — Tier 1 official commentary / regulator analytical position.

title: AI Will Reshape More Jobs Than It Replaces
key_claim: BCG microeconomic model: 50-55% of US jobs (~165M, BLS Jan 2026) will be reshaped by AI within 2-3 years; 10-15% (16-25M) could be eliminated within 5 years; workforce strategy must move upstream into corporate strategy rather than sit downstream of automation.

title: Research: How AI Is Changing the Labor Market
key_claim: Underlying HBS Working Paper 25-039 (Chen, Srinivasan, Zakerinia): generative AI cuts 17% of job postings in automation-heavy roles while increasing demand by 22% in human-AI collaboration positions; 24% decrease in AI-exposed skills per firm per quarter for top-quartile automation-exposed jobs; 15% increase in AI-exposed skills for augmentation-exposed jobs.
notes: Tier 2 institutional research — HBR article based on Harvard Business School academic working paper.

title: AI won't kill your job — it will kill the path to your first one
key_claim: Fortune coverage (Yale CELI / Sonnenfeld): biggest AI-on-jobs impact will not be visible layoffs but opportunities that never materialise — entry-level positions that quietly disappear; workers aged 22-25 in AI-exposed roles have seen a 16% drop in employment; US companies adopting AI reducing hiring of junior employees by ~13%.
notes: Tier 3 quality journalism; corroborates broader pattern that traditional career-entry pipeline is breaking under AI.

title: 41% of Organizations Have Hired a Fake Candidate (GetReal Security Deepfake Readiness Benchmark Report)
key_claim: GetReal Security survey of 668 IT/cyber/risk/fraud leaders (Sept 2025, organisations 1,000+ employees): 41% report having hired and onboarded a fraudulent candidate; 88% encounter deepfake or impersonation attacks at least occasionally; 45% report frequent attacks. Only 35% list fake candidates as primary concern despite the 41% incidence — large awareness gap.
notes: Structural anchor for the verification-crisis framing; 5 months old but canonical baseline empirical work on enterprise hiring fraud.

title: How Employers Are Confronting Deepfake Interview Fraud
key_claim: SHRM coverage notes Experian's 2026 Future of Fraud Forecast lists deepfake job candidates among top 5 fraud threats; Gartner forecast that by end-2026 ~30% of enterprises will find standard identity verification cannot reliably distinguish real face from deepfake; CBS News study: 50% of businesses encountered AI-driven deepfake fraud; InCruiter detection found fraud in 25-30% of flagged sessions vs. ~half that for human interviewers.
notes: Tier 3 industry-association quality coverage; SHRM is HR profession's standard-setter.

title: SkillsTX acquires Credentials Cloud for AI-native, evidence-based credential verification
key_claim: SkillsTX acquisition of Credentials Cloud (4 Feb 2026) explicitly positions evidence-based credential verification (Open Badge 3.0, SFIA-aligned, cryptographically signed, real-time verification API) as the response to AI-augmented hiring fraud; piloted at University of Canberra and embedded in SkillsTX Talent eXperience platform.
notes: Tier 4 vendor source — directional. Documents the supplier-side response (cryptographic credential verification as a category) corroborating the broader pattern.
